sources.entry: Gotify - Notification server with Android and CLI clients (alternative to PushBullet). (Source Code, Clients) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Gotify Android is the Android client app for the gotify/server push notification server, showing notifications for new messages and letting you view and delete them.
summary.what_it_does: The app connects to a gotify/server instance and displays push notifications when new messages arrive. Users can view messages within the app and delete them. Notification behavior is mapped to message priority: priority 0 produces no notification, 1-3 shows a status bar icon, 4-7 adds sound, and 8-10 adds vibration. The README also covers keeping the app alive by disabling battery optimization, and minimizing the persistent foreground connection-status notification on Android 8 and later. The project is built with Gradle and uses an OpenAPI generator to update the client code from the server API.
use_cases: receive push notifications from a self-hosted server on Android
view and delete server messages on a phone
replace PushBullet-style notifications with a self-hosted service
set notification sound and vibration by message priority
keep a notification app running under battery optimization
how_to_run: Download the APK, or install Gotify from F-Droid or Google Play
Build the APK with Java 17 using: ./gradlew build
To regenerate the API client, run: ./gradlew openApiGenerate
notable: Message priority maps to notification behavior: sound at 4-7, vibration at 8-10
Connects to a self-hosted gotify/server instance rather than a hosted cloud service
Available via APK download, F-Droid, or Google Play
Client API code is regenerated from the server's OpenAPI spec
caveats: Android only; the app needs battery optimization disabled to receive notifications reliably
Requires a running gotify/server instance to connect to
Foreground connection notification is only minimizable on Android 8 and later
